name.text: Finding the mistake in the inequalities of a region

questiontext.text:

generalfeedback.text:
(a) Inequality ({@wi@}) is wrong. [[if test="is(ek=\"rev\")"]]It describes the shaded side, which is the unwanted one.[[elif test="is(ek=\"strict\")"]]Its sign does not match the line: line {@wi@} is [[if test="strictp(Lw[4])"]]dashed[[else]]solid[[/if]].[[else]]Its boundary crosses the axes in the wrong places: line {@wi@} is {@lind(Lw[1], Lw[2], Lw[3])@}.[[/if]] Test with a point in \(R\), such as \(({@nd(G[1])@}, {@nd(G[2])@})\), the centre of the triangle.

(b) The correct inequality is {@rd@}.

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: finding the mistake in the inequalities of a region

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Find the wrong inequality in a description of a clear region and write it correctly.

Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: One is wrong. Test a point in \(R\) in each inequality, and check each line's style and crossings.

falsefeedback.text: Inequality ({@chs@}), {@wd[chs]@}, is right. Test it with a point in \(R\), such as {@tpd@}: {@gst@} is true. Its sign also matches line {@chs@}, which is [[if test="strictp(W[chs][4])"]]dashed[[else]]solid[[/if]]. Check the others.

[[if test="is(lkind(Lw)=\"vertical\")"]]Line {@wi@} is vertical: every point on it has \(x = {@Lw[3]@}\), so its inequality uses only \(x\).[[elif test="is(lkind(Lw)=\"horizontal\")"]]Line {@wi@} is horizontal: every point on it has \(y = {@Lw[3]@}\), so its inequality uses only \(y\).[[else]]Line {@wi@} is sloping, so its inequality needs both \(x\) and \(y\).[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: That is Wafula's inequality, the one with the mistake.

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="lsame and lside"]]Your inequality is now on the right side of line {@wi@}. Test it with a point in \(R\), such as {@tpd@}.[[elif test="llin"]]Your inequality has {@lbd@} as its boundary, which is not line {@wi@}.
